findings.title: With sync enabled, `res.data` is undefined on the fetch Response, so the Google refresh crashes.
findings.body: When sync is on, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a WHATWG fetch `Response`, while the non-sync path returns the googleapis/gaxios response that has `.data`. A fetch `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. Every Google token refresh for synced users fails. Fix: in the sync path of `refreshOAuthTokens`, check `response.ok` and return parsed JSON, and have every caller handle the same shape.

findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse result object instead of the token data.
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `SafeParseReturn` (`{ success, data }`). The old code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse()`, which returns the data itself. Now `{ key }` writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into `credential.key` on every Google token refresh, whether or not sync is enabled. The next read of the credential no longer has `access_token`/`refresh_token` at the top level, so the Google integration breaks. Fix: use `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`.

findings.title: With sync enabled, HubSpot saves a raw fetch Response as the credential.
findings.body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, not a HubSpot `TokenResponseIF`. `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined, so `expiryDate` becomes NaN, and the `Response` object (not the token JSON) is written to `credential.key`. The HubSpot credential is corrupted on the first refresh. Fix: parse the sync response's JSON and map it to the HubSpot token shape before using it.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every client creation, ignores sync, and keeps using the old access token.
findings.body: `getClient` now always POSTs a refresh to login.salesforce.com, even when the token is still valid. It never goes through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the self-hosted sync endpoint is never used. It also throws whenever `statusText !== "OK"`, and statusText can be empty, for example over HTTP/2. After saving the new token, the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the stale `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`. In sync mode the minimum schema also strips `instance_url` from the stored key. Fix: refresh only when needed, check `response.ok`, go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, and build the connection from the refreshed token.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService.
findings.body: The file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include `@calcom/prisma`, yet `getClient` now calls `prisma.credential.update`. The file fails type-checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime when a Salesforce client is built. Fix: `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential id as the user id, and reads `.data` from a fetch Response.
findings.body: `credentialId` is passed where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects a userId. The sync endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>` and returns tokens for the wrong user, or for none. Separately, in sync mode the result is a fetch `Response`, so `tokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError. Fix: pass the credential's `userId`, and normalise the sync response into the shape the caller expects.

findings.title: The computed keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` do not validate an expiry field.
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal string "[object Object]", so both computed keys are the same property. The schema ends up as `{ access_token, "[object Object]": unknown().optional() }`, which requires no numeric expiry. Because z.object strips unknown keys, it also removes `expires_in`/`expiry_date` from the parsed data. Callers that use `parsed.data` (Zoom, Office365, Salesforce) lose the expiry, so tokens look permanently expired or get NaN expiries. Fix: use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` and validate the expiry field explicitly.

findings.title: With sync enabled, Zoho CRM reads `.data` from a fetch Response and throws.
findings.body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, which has no `.data`. `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` therefore throws, and every Zoho CRM refresh fails for synced users. Fix: return parsed JSON in a consistent shape from `refreshOAuthTokens`, or adapt the caller.

findings.title: The webhook secret is checked with a non-constant-time comparison, and the endpoint accepts any HTTP method.
findings.body: This endpoint lets a caller write OAuth credentials for any userId. The `!==` string comparison leaks timing information about the secret. The handler also accepts GET and any other method. Fix: compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (after checking lengths and that the header is a single string), and reject requests that are not POST. A malformed body or a failed decrypt also throws a 500 from `parse`/`JSON.parse`; use `safeParse` and return 400.

findings.title: A placeholder `"refresh_token"` string replaces the real refresh token when the response omits one.
findings.body: If the response has no `refresh_token` (always in sync mode, and allowed by providers such as Microsoft), the data gets the literal `"refresh_token"`. Office365 then spreads this into `o365AuthCredentials` and saves it, overwriting the stored real refresh token. If sync is later disabled, the credential cannot refresh. Fix: do not inject a placeholder; keep the existing refresh token when the response omits one.

findings.title: An Office365 token-parse failure now throws, where before it was logged and the refresh continued.
findings.body: The old code logged the zod error with the MS response and still saved the merged credentials. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws a generic error, so the diagnostic logging is gone and any schema mismatch aborts calendar operations. The `tokenResponse.success &&` guard is now dead code. If throwing is intended, at least keep the logging of the zod error.

held.title: An unrelated hardcoding of the Zoho Bigin redirect URI slug.
held.body: The redirect URI changed from `appConfig.slug` to the literal `zoho-bigin`, which the credential-sync request does not cover. If `config.json`'s slug differs from `zoho-bigin`, the redirect no longer matches the one the callback uses, and OAuth fails. Revert to `appConfig.slug`.
